/LILIAN

Baltic Exchange Market Report 12 May 2026
Baltic Dry Index: 3063 (62)
Baltic Capesize Index: 5082 (106)
Baltic Panamax Index: 2360 (77)
Baltic Supramax Index: 1535 (8)
Baltic Handysize Index: 843 (5)
CAPESIZE
A slightly mixed day, with the Pacific remaining broadly flat while sentiment in the Atlantic basin continued to show signs of improvement. Despite limited upside on the key Pacific routes, firmer Atlantic activity and stronger trans-Atlantic demand helped support overall market levels. The BCI 182 5TC increased by $958 to settle at $46,091. C5 remained relatively flat, easing marginally by 0.040 to $15.175, while C3 edged up by $0.122 to $35.736. In the Pacific, conditions were described as balanced but lacking fresh momentum. Two miners were active on C5 today, although this was not enough to materially shift sentiment. Early offers were reportedly in the mid-to-upper $15s, with fixtures heard around $15.00-$15.05, before market talk emerged of a miner paying $15.15 on a Newcastlemax, although this remained unconfirmed. The Atlantic basin showed more encouraging signs, particularly on trans-Atlantic business, with stronger activity pushing the C8 index up by $3,706 to $52,925. On C3, bids were said to be improving, with market talk of $35 being bid on index dates and closer to $36 for 15 June onwards, against offers around $37.00.
PANAMAX
Market sources have once again highlighted the confidence being echoed across both basins. The Atlantic is said to exemplify this positive sentiment, with the upward trend in offers largely attributed to the strength in fronthaul rates. Brokers note that cargo flows and trading activity on trans Atlantic routes remain relatively thin, however, with demand for tonnage heading East becoming increasingly evident owners are said to be advancing their rate ideas should they consider shorter duration Atlantic business. Fronthaul activity remains robust, with both the US East Coast and North Coast South America highlighted as particularly strong regions. Increased tonnage demand is also playing a key role in absorbing and consequently tightening the availability of prompt tonnage, particularly in the North Atlantic. In the Pacific, market participants have pointed to limited prompt tonnage availability alongside an improving North Pacific grains market. This, coupled with strong mineral supply from Indonesia and Australia, is contributing to a near-term market trajectory that appears to be strengthening day by day. Messrs Jera were reported to have fixed the Blue Ridge (82,099 2013), open Panjin on 16 May, for an East Coast Australia round trip at $24,500. Meanwhile the Ikan Belanak (81,609 2020) open Sual 14/15 May was also reported fixed for an East Coast Australia trip to Singapore-Japan, with the rate concluded in the region of $28,500–$29,000. The P5TC’s improvement today of $693, bringing it to $21,241, further reinforces the positive sentiment shared by many industry participants.
SUPRAMAX
Another positional day for the sector. The Atlantic had a rather lacklustre feel, although some felt that demand from the South Atlantic had improved certainly for fronthaul business. The Continent-Mediterranean was said to still be lacking fresh enquiry, whilst the Gulf continued on its gentle upward trajectory. The Asian arena was a bit more buoyant, and sentiment remained positive in most quarters. The 11TC average finished the day up $108 at $19,408.

Atlantic
The Bulk Atacama (61,384 2014) open Dunkirk 17/19 May was heard fixed at $10,750 for a trip via ARAG redelivery EC Mexico with fertilisers. A 57,000 was heard fixed basis delivery EC South America trip redelivery Port Louis at $15,000 plus $500,000 ballast bonus. It surfaced that recently the Lowlands Angel (61,239 2019) was fixed basis delivery New Orleans 9 May for an inter Caribbean business at $23,000. The Pacific Victory (63,508 2017) was also heard fixed SW Pass trip Spain with grains at $25,500 to ADM.

Asia
The African Goldeneye (58,110 2012) open Philippines was heard fixed in the low $19.000s for a trip to the Far East but no more details surfaced. The Vosco Ocean a 58,000, Vosco new purchase open Qinhuangdao was heard fixed with steel coils to Vietnam at $19,500, but no more details came to light.

HANDYSIZE
It was another quiet session in the Handy market, with overall sentiment remaining largely positional. Across the Continent and Mediterranean, the tonnage list is still lengthy for May dates, while new enquiry remains limited. The US Gulf market was broadly steady, whereas the South Atlantic continued to firm on the back of emerging fresh demand. In Asia, conditions were stable, with a balanced cargo-to-tonnage ratio supporting a positive rate trend. The Shinsung Accord (37,063 2015), open Oita 16 May, fixed at around $21,000 for a trip to WC India, although further details were not disclosed. The Ocean Flora (37,609 2019), open CJK 18/23 May, fixed for SE Asia with Indonesia intended at about $18,000, again with no additional details reported. All these were reflected on index with the 7TC average up $88 to close at $15,165.

Market Fundamentals
Middle East and Gas Uncertainty Drives Richards Bay High

The thermal coal market at Richards Bay reached its highest point in two months, fuelled by escalating natural gas prices and uncertainty surrounding Middle East peace negotiations, according to McCloskey. As of May 11, the Richards Bay 6,000 kc NAR price was assessed at $118.04/t FOB, the highest since March. The weekly average reached $114.79/t FOB, marking the highest weekly average observed since November 2023. In the year to 6 May, South African coal exports rose 9.2% from the same period last year to 25.6 Mt, vessel tracking data show.

Trading Commentary
Cape
The Cape FFA curve moved significantly higher today in response to a firmer Atlantic market, specifically C8/C9 and C3. The biggest move was on the May and Jun contracts with 41900 and 38000 paid, followed by Jul with 34950 trading. The May v Jun spread remained relatively unchanged with 3750 implied for most of the day. Q3 and Q4 made significant gains also with 33500 and 32300 trading respectively. Cal27 was a little more stable trading up to 26500 and similarly the Cal28 with 23400 trading.

PMX
PMX had another active day with rates pushing higher across the whole of the curve, with the front being well supported by physical strength. May traded up from 21400 to 22000, while June was again the main interest of the day, trading in a wide range of 22400–23550 closing around that level. July printed 21600–22750 in around 1800 lots, with August also firmer at 20875–21700. Further out, Q3 traded actively between 20800 and 21700, while the Q3+Q4 strip was paid 20000–20250. Q4 also moved higher from 18550–19250. Cal 27 traded 15325–15700, with Cal 28 at 14125–14275 in large volume and Cal 29 steady around 13650–13725.

SMX + HANDY
Momentum continued to build across the SMX curve, with another well supported session seeing prices extend up, reaching fresh highs across the board. May traded from 18050 to 18300 and while Jun made substantial gains, trading actively from 18850 up to a high of 19750. Jul was well bid, traded 19000 to 19600, while Aug traded in a tighter range of 18650 to 18700. Q3 traded actively from 18300 to 18850, the Q3+Q4 strip cleared at 17600 and Q4 traded from 16400 to 16850. Further out, Liquidity on Cal27 was robust, trading 13525 to 13800 and Cal28 traded 12325 to 12500. Support was sustained in the Handy market, May trading 15450, Jun at 16200, Jul at 16100 and Q3 at 15300.

Carbon
EU carbon markets opened �0.50/eua lower, maintaining this level throughout most of the morning before selling off as energy prices rose on renewed Middle East concerns. Prompt month TTF gas prices have moved into the mid �46/MWh range, threatening EU industrial gas demand and thereby undermining demand for EUAs. Today's EU Common auction settled at �75.00/eua, significantly below last night's daily futures spot close and further pressuring EUA futures markets. During the assessment window, the benchmark Dec26 contract was trading at �75.77/eua, down 1.9%, and on close to average volume.

Market Fundamentals
Middle East and Gas Uncertainty Drives Richards Bay
High
The thermal coal market at Richards Bay reached its highest
point in two months, fuelled by escalating natural gas prices
and uncertainty surrounding Middle East peace negotiations,
according to McCloskey. As of May 11, the Richards Bay 6,000
kc NAR price was assessed at $118.04/t FOB, the highest
since March. The weekly average reached $114.79/t FOB,
marking the highest weekly average observed since
November 2023. In the year to 6 May, South African coal
exports rose 9.2% from the same period last year to 25.6 Mt,
vessel tracking data show.
Trading Commentary
Cape
The Cape FFA curve moved signiﬁcantly higher today in
response to a ﬁrmer Atlantic market, speciﬁcally C8/C9 and
C3. The biggest move was on the May and Jun contracts with
41900 and 38000 paid, followed by Jul with 34950 trading.
The May v Jun spread remained relatively unchanged with
3750 implied for most of the day. Q3 and Q4 made
signiﬁcant gains also with 33500 and 32300 trading
respectively. Cal27 was a little more stable trading up to
26500 and similarly the Cal28 with 23400 trading.
PMX
PMX had another active day with rates pushing higher across
the whole of the curve, with the front being well supported
by physical strength. May traded up from 21400 to 22000,
while June was again the main interest of the day, trading in
a wide range of 22400–23550 closing around that level. July
printed 21600–22750 in around 1800 lots, with August also
ﬁrmer at 20875–21700. Further out, Q3 traded actively
between 20800 and 21700, while the Q3+Q4 strip was paid
20000–20250. Q4 also moved higher from 18550–19250. Cal
27 traded 15325–15700, with Cal 28 at 14125–14275 in large
volume and Cal 29 steady around 13650–13725.
SMX + HANDY
Momentum continued to build across the SMX curve, with
another well supported session seeing prices extend up,
reaching fresh highs across the board. May traded from
18050 to 18300 and while Jun made substantial gains,
trading actively from 18850 up to a high of 19750. Jul was
well bid, traded 19000 to 19600, while Aug traded in a tighter
range of 18650 to 18700. Q3 traded actively from 18300 to
18850, the Q3+Q4 strip cleared at 17600 and Q4 traded from
16400 to 16850. Further out, Liquidity on Cal27 was robust,
trading 13525 to 13800 and Cal28 traded 12325 to 12500.
Support was sustained in the Handy market, May trading
15450, Jun at 16200, Jul at 16100 and Q3 at 15300.Cape 180 5TC

Capesize Report12th May 2026
PAC: Flat         ATL: Strong
Market Comments
Tuesday was welcomed to a lift in demand in the Paciﬁc basin as four majors
were seen to be present. It wasn’t long before oﬀers in the mid $15s region
were pushed by owners, however majors were patient before engaging. One
Hedland major seemed reluctant to engage oﬀers received in the low/mid $15s
region, whilst the Dampier major was seen to take a handful of stems between
27/30 May at a $15.00-15 range. One miner out of Hay Point was seen to
promptly ﬁx their early June backhaul stem to Rotterdam, though rates are
unclear at this time. Out of Indonesia, the usual operator ﬁxed their stem to
Mundra in the mid $12s for 18/24 May. Finally, the major out of TRMT ﬁxed a
trip to Qingdao for 25/27 May sub $12s. Focus continued to focus on early/mid
June dates in the South Atlantic as demand remains strong against a moderate
tonnage. Initially, bids came in at $35's for early and mid June - however, a
ﬁxture reported at $36.25 C3 for 06/13 June ﬁxture helped prompt up the basin.
Into the afternoon, bids rose closer to owners ideas to mid $36.00's for mid
June dates as an 11/20 June stem ﬁxed $36.85 C3 and mid $36.00's were also
ﬁxed for 06/12 June dates and mid June dates a couple of times. All in all, a
strong end to the day as the basin ﬁrmed up. A busy start in the North Atlantic
this week after a handful of ﬁxtures were conducted yesterday. Into this
afternoon, stem from Drummond to South Korea was seen holding a $48's
oﬀer for end June dates, whilst one vessel caught attraction from West African
bids as stems continue to price well for North vessels. All in all, the North
remains ﬁrm as fronthaul and transatlantic stems remain in focus for both
halves of June.

CARGO DEMAND AND TIGHTENING VESSEL SUPPLY, SHOULD CREATE THE IDEAL CONDITIONS FOR THE
PANAMAX ATLANTIC MARKET TO MAINTAIN ITS UPWARD TRAJECTORY AT LEAST THROUGH TOMORROW’S
CLOSE. HOWEVER, HOLIDAYS ON THURSDAY AND FRIDAY MAY RESULT IN A QUIETER END TO THE WEEK
PAC SHORT:
THE PACIFIC MARKET HAS STARTED THE WEEK ON A PRETTY FIRM FOOTING, WITH SENTIMENT REMAINING
POSITIVE AMID HEALTHY CARGO ACTIVITY AND CONTINUED UPWARD PRESSURE ON RATES. CARGO
COUNTS HAVE IMPROVED ACROSS THE BOARD, WHILE THE TONNAGE LIST REMAINS RELATIVELY BALANCED
DESPITE A SLIGHT INCREASE IN AVAILABLE VESSELS, KEEPING OVERALL MARKET CONDITIONS SUPPORTIVE
FOR OWNERS. AUSSIE HAS SHOWN THE STRONGEST MOMENTUM THIS WEEK, WITH AUS RVS BEING FIXED
AROUND THE MID HIGH $24,000 TO $25,000 BKI CJK LEVELS AS STRONG FIXING ACTIVITY AND FRESH EARLY
JUNE DEMAND CONTINUE TO SUPPORT SENTIMENT. NOPAC HAS ALSO CONTINUED TO STRENGTHEN,
SUPPORTED BY FRESH GRAIN AND COAL STEMS FOR EARLY JUNE ALONGSIDE SOME OUTSTANDING END
MAY CARGOES, WITH P3 NOW ALSO BEING SEEN FIXING AROUND THE $24,000 LEVELS FOR NOPAC. INDO
DEMAND HAS IMPROVED COMPARED TO LAST WEEK, PARTICULARLY FOR LATER MAY DATES, WHILE
LIMESTONE BUSINESS EX SCHINA/INDIA CONTINUES TO GENERATE A FAIR AMOUNT OF ENQUIRY.
FOLLOWING THE STRONG FIXING ACTIVITY SEEN AT THE START OF THE WEEK AND THE SHARP PUSH IN
RATES, SOME CHARTERERS HAVE BEEN SEEN HOLDING BACK ON BIDS AND TAKING A MORE CAUTIOUS
APPROACH WHILE REASSESSING MARKET DIRECTION. ON THE SUPPLY SIDE, TONNAGE AVAILABILITY HAS
INCREASED SLIGHTLY BOTH IN THE NORTH AND SOUTH, THOUGH THE SPOT MARKET STILL APPEARS
RELATIVELY TIGHT OVERALL AND HAS NOT SHIFTED BARGAINING POWER BACK TOWARD CHARTERERS.

Handysize/Supramax Report12th May 2026
63,500 Atlantic: FLAT      Paciﬁc: FIRMER           38,000 Atlantic: FLAT      Paciﬁc: FIRMER
Market Comments
ATLANTIC:
While the the Handysize Continent market remains relatively quiet we have seen a 40,000
deadweight vessel open Antwerp rated $15,000 for a Fronthaul trip as well as a 39,000 deadweight
vessel ﬁx basis delivery Rouen for a trip to Morocco at $13,250 – both slightly softer levels than we
have previously seen. For the larger sizes, ﬁxing levels for a transatlantic voyage are down
marginally at $10,250.
In the Mediterranean market, activity remains muted as limited enquiry continues to fail to match a
long tonnage list for both the smaller and larger sizes. For the Handysize vessels, ﬁxing levels for a
transatlantic voyage have softened to $8,500. In the Supramax/Ultramax Mediterranean market,
we saw a 55,000 deadweight vessel rated at $10,000 for a trip from the West Mediterranean to
West Africa.
The ECSA market started the week with a clear split in momentum, as Ultramaxes are pushing
higher on the back of a tightening Panamax segment, with eco-large units now commanding rates
reaching toward USD 19,000 + USD 900,000 GBB for Far East fronthauls and exceeding USD 30,000
for ECSA Transatlantic trips. While the larger geared vessels capitalize on this strength, the
Handysize sector has remained comparatively ﬂat, starting the week with limited fresh activity.
In the Handyszie US Gulf market Week opened with oﬀer/demand balance remaining generally
steady across for TAs, inter-Caribs and WCCA cargoes for second half May. Reported ﬁxing levels
continue in line with previous done, while discussions for end-May positions still show some gaps
between charterers’ ideas and owners’ expectations, though nothing outside the normal.
Grain/export activity out of the USG continues to provide underlying support for prompt
employment and tonnage supply for prompt/mid-May dates still appears manageable, preventing
charterers from gaining any real leverage despite some softer testing here and there. Overall
sentiment remains fairly balanced for now. For the Supramax/Ultramax sizes, the week started on a
quiet note with the slightly lower levels continuing. One 64 dwt ﬁxed Del miss river trip Ec Mex at a
shade under $20,000 with grains for 20-25 May and another Ultra 61 dwt was close to ﬁxing a
steady level of $25,000 to Asia with Grains but was not yet fully concluded. Overall the market
today felt positive though heading towards end May as there are also more USEC orders showing.
PACIFIC:
SEA started the week quietly, with overall performance relatively ﬂat. EKALI coal cargoes were
abundant but vessel supply was tight, with tonnage concentrated mostly in the west side, meaning
rates there stayed ﬂat, while the east still managed to see some good numbers. Contrary to most
people's expectations last week, the SEA market did not see a signiﬁcant improvement this week,
with the China direction notably weaker than the SEA direction. On Monday, it was heard that an
SMX open in KSC ﬁxed at 13K back to China, but it was said that the vessel required DD and had
limited options. In the Aussie direction, some cargoes were still waiting to be covered, but oﬀers
were not aggressive, with a charterer calculating 20K for a Southeast Asia-based UMX.
In the north, the general cargo segment was very active, especially for back haul cargoes to Africa
or the Med. Vessels able to transit Goa could still get a decent premium. It was reported a charterer
calculated 24k DOP for a UMX open in NChina. Early this week, it was also heard that a UMX ﬁxed at
20K to WAfrica. Due to limited vessel supply, some charterers opted to take vessels on period basis.
Several high period ﬁxtures were seen this week, with levels reaching around 19kish for 1yr. The
Nopac market was relatively less hot, but still felt to be rising, with many UMX vessels achieving
around 18kish DOP for Nopac grain.
In ECI, some vessels remains this week, with a UMX fetching around 16kish DOP for ECI cargo back
to China. The WCI direction was generally ﬂat. Some market cargoes emerged chasing vessels, but
oﬀers were limited, with a SMX for local WCI cargo back to China around 12K. The SAfrica market
had considerable cargo volumes, with oﬀers for a UMX for PACIFIC-bound cargo around 21K+210K.
In summary, regional performance showed signiﬁcant diﬀerences, with SEA ﬂat but the north
active.
We look forward to seeing how the market performs going forward.

items.parsed_text: Capesize Report12th May 2026 PAC: Flat ATL: Strong Market Comments Tuesday was welcomed to a lift in demand in the Pacific basin as four majors were seen to be present. It wasn’t long before offers in the mid $15s region were pushed by owners, however majors were patient before engaging. One Hedland major seemed reluctant to engage offers received in the low/mid $15s region, whilst the Dampier major was seen to take a handful of stems between 27/30 May at a $15.00-15 range. One miner out of Hay Point was seen to promptly fix their early June backhaul stem to Rotterdam, though rates are unclear at this time. Out of Indonesia, the usual operator fixed their stem to Mundra in the mid $12s for 18/24 May. Finally, the major out of TRMT fixed a trip to Qingdao for 25/27 May sub $12s. Focus continued to focus on early/mid June dates in the South Atlantic as demand remains strong against a moderate tonnage. Initially, bids came in at $35's for early and mid June - however, a fixture reported at $36.25 C3 for 06/13 June fixture helped prompt up the basin. Into the afternoon, bids rose closer to owners ideas to mid $36.00's for mid June dates as an 11/20 June stem fixed $36.85 C3 and mid $36.00's were also fixed for 06/12 June dates and mid June dates a couple of times. All in all, a strong end to the day as the basin firmed up. A busy start in the North Atlantic this week after a handful of fixtures were conducted yesterday. Into this afternoon, stem from Drummond to South Korea was seen holding a $48's offer for end June dates, whilst one vessel caught attraction from West African bids as stems continue to price well for North vessels. All in all, the North remains firm as fronthaul and transatlantic stems remain in focus for both halves of June. items.parsed_text: Panam ax/Kamsarmax Report12th May 2026 ATL: FIRM PAC: FIRM MID EAST: FIRM Market Comments ATL SHORT: 1A - MONDAY AND TUESDAY’S SESSIONS BROUGHT FIRMER FIXING LEVELS AND INCREASED OFFERS. WE ENTERED THE WEEK ON MONDAY WITH MARKET VALUE SUGGESTED TO BE AROUND $18K FOR A TA ROUND VOYAGE. BY TUESDAY EVENING, THIS HAD INCREASED BY AT LEAST $2K PER DAY, WITH THE ROUTE NOW EXPECTED TO COMMAND RATES BEGINNING WITH AT LEAST '2' INFRONT FOR OWNERS (BSS BKI ALGECIRAS). 2A - SIMILAR TO THE 1A ROUTE, WE HAVE CONTINUED TO SEE TIGHT TONNAGE LISTS ALONGSIDE EXPANDING CARGO DEMAND. THIS SUPPLY-DEMAND IMBALANCE HAS LEFT OWNERS FIRMLY IN THE DRIVING SEAT, ALLOWING THEM TO PUSH OFFERS HIGHER AFTER EACH FRESH FIXTURE. ON MONDAY, FAIR VALUE WAS CONSIDERED TO BE AROUND $27,500, BUT WE ARE NOW SEEING MULTIPLE FIXTURES BEING CONCLUDED AT $30K BKI ALGECIRAS EQUIVLENT FOR FRONTHAUL BUSINESS. P6 - DESPITE SLOWER FIXING VOLUMES AND ULTRAMAX VESSELS CONTINUING TO UNDERCUT PANAMAXES ON GRAIN BUSINESS, MOMENTUM REMAINS FIRMLY UPWARD FOR OWNERS. REPORTED FIXTURES INDICATE A NOTABLE INCREASE FROM LAST WEEK’S HIGHS, WITH CURRENT MARKET LEVELS ASSESSED AROUND $21,500 - 22,000. OUTLOOK - A FIRM CAPE MARKET AND A STRENGTHENING PACIFIC MARKET, COMBINED WITH CONTINUED CARGO DEMAND AND TIGHTENING VESSEL SUPPLY, SHOULD CREATE THE IDEAL CONDITIONS FOR THE PANAMAX ATLANTIC MARKET TO MAINTAIN ITS UPWARD TRAJECTORY AT LEAST THROUGH TOMORROW’S CLOSE. HOWEVER, HOLIDAYS ON THURSDAY AND FRIDAY MAY RESULT IN A QUIETER END TO THE WEEK PAC SHORT: THE PACIFIC MARKET HAS STARTED THE WEEK ON A PRETTY FIRM FOOTING, WITH SENTIMENT REMAINING POSITIVE AMID HEALTHY CARGO ACTIVITY AND CONTINUED UPWARD PRESSURE ON RATES. CARGO COUNTS HAVE IMPROVED ACROSS THE BOARD, WHILE THE TONNAGE LIST REMAINS RELATIVELY BALANCED DESPITE A SLIGHT INCREASE IN AVAILABLE VESSELS, KEEPING OVERALL MARKET CONDITIONS SUPPORTIVE FOR OWNERS. AUSSIE HAS SHOWN THE STRONGEST MOMENTUM THIS WEEK, WITH AUS RVS BEING FIXED AROUND THE MID HIGH $24,000 TO $25,000 BKI CJK LEVELS AS STRONG FIXING ACTIVITY AND FRESH EARLY JUNE DEMAND CONTINUE TO SUPPORT SENTIMENT. NOPAC HAS ALSO CONTINUED TO STRENGTHEN, SUPPORTED BY FRESH GRAIN AND COAL STEMS FOR EARLY JUNE ALONGSIDE SOME OUTSTANDING END MAY CARGOES, WITH P3 NOW ALSO BEING SEEN FIXING AROUND THE $24,000 LEVELS FOR NOPAC. INDO DEMAND HAS IMPROVED COMPARED TO LAST WEEK, PARTICULARLY FOR LATER MAY DATES, WHILE LIMESTONE BUSINESS EX SCHINA/INDIA CONTINUES TO GENERATE A FAIR AMOUNT OF ENQUIRY. FOLLOWING THE STRONG FIXING ACTIVITY SEEN AT THE START OF THE WEEK AND THE SHARP PUSH IN RATES, SOME CHARTERERS HAVE BEEN SEEN HOLDING BACK ON BIDS AND TAKING A MORE CAUTIOUS APPROACH WHILE REASSESSING MARKET DIRECTION. ON THE SUPPLY SIDE, TONNAGE AVAILABILITY HAS INCREASED SLIGHTLY BOTH IN THE NORTH AND SOUTH, THOUGH THE SPOT MARKET STILL APPEARS RELATIVELY TIGHT OVERALL AND HAS NOT SHIFTED BARGAINING POWER BACK TOWARD CHARTERERS. HOWEVER, HOLIDAYS ON THURSDAY AND FRIDAY MAY RESULT IN A QUIETER END TO THE WEEK PAC SHORT: THE PACIFIC MARKET HAS STARTED THE WEEK ON A PRETTY FIRM FOOTING, WITH SENTIMENT REMAINING POSITIVE AMID HEALTHY CARGO ACTIVITY AND CONTINUED UPWARD PRESSURE ON RATES. NOW ALSO BEING SEEN FIXING AROUND THE $24,000 LEVELS FOR NOPAC. INDO DEMAND HAS IMPROVED COMPARED TO LAST WEEK, PARTICULARLY FOR LATER MAY DATES, WHILE LIMESTONE BUSINESS EX SCHINA/INDIA CONTINUES TO GENERATE A FAIR AMOUNT OF ENQUIRY. FOLLOWING THE STRONG FIXING ACTIVITY SEEN AT THE START OF THE WEEK AND THE SHARP PUSH IN RATES, SOME CHARTERERS HAVE BEEN SEEN HOLDING BACK ON BIDS AND TAKING A MORE CAUTIOUS APPROACH WHILE REASSESSING MARKET DIRECTION. ON THE SUPPLY SIDE, TONNAGE AVAILABILITY HAS INCREASED SLIGHTLY BOTH IN THE NORTH AND SOUTH, THOUGH THE SPOT MARKET STILL APPEARS RELATIVELY TIGHT OVERALL AND HAS NOT SHIFTED BARGAINING POWER BACK TOWARD CHARTERERS. items.parsed_text: Handysize/Supramax Report12th May 2026 63,500 Atlantic: FLAT Pacific: FIRMER 38,000 Atlantic: FLAT Pacific: FIRMER Market Comments ATLANTIC: While the the Handysize Continent market remains relatively quiet we have seen a 40,000 deadweight vessel open Antwerp rated $15,000 for a Fronthaul trip as well as a 39,000 deadweight vessel fix basis delivery Rouen for a trip to Morocco at $13,250 – both slightly softer levels than we have previously seen. For the larger sizes, fixing levels for a transatlantic voyage are down marginally at $10,250. In the Mediterranean market, activity remains muted as limited enquiry continues to fail to match a long tonnage list for both the smaller and larger sizes. For the Handysize vessels, fixing levels for a transatlantic voyage have softened to $8,500. In the Supramax/Ultramax Mediterranean market, we saw a 55,000 deadweight vessel rated at $10,000 for a trip from the West Mediterranean to West Africa. The ECSA market started the week with a clear split in momentum, as Ultramaxes are pushing higher on the back of a tightening Panamax segment, with eco-large units now commanding rates reaching toward USD 19,000 + USD 900,000 GBB for Far East fronthauls and exceeding USD 30,000 for ECSA Transatlantic trips. While the larger geared vessels capitalize on this strength, the Handysize sector has remained comparatively flat, starting the week with limited fresh activity. In the Handyszie US Gulf market Week opened with offer/demand balance remaining generally steady across for TAs, inter-Caribs and WCCA cargoes for second half May. Reported fixing levels continue in line with previous done, while discussions for end-May positions still show some gaps between charterers’ ideas and owners’ expectations, though nothing outside the normal. Grain/export activity out of the USG continues to provide underlying support for prompt employment and tonnage supply for prompt/mid-May dates still appears manageable, preventing charterers from gaining any real leverage despite some softer testing here and there. Overall sentiment remains fairly balanced for now. For the Supramax/Ultramax sizes, the week started on a quiet note with the slightly lower levels continuing. One 64 dwt fixed Del miss river trip Ec Mex at a shade under $20,000 with grains for 20-25 May and another Ultra 61 dwt was close to fixing a steady level of $25,000 to Asia with Grains but was not yet fully concluded. Overall the market today felt positive though heading towards end May as there are also more USEC orders showing. PACIFIC: SEA started the week quietly, with overall performance relatively flat. EKALI coal cargoes were abundant but vessel supply was tight, with tonnage concentrated mostly in the west side, meaning rates there stayed flat, while the east still managed to see some good numbers. Contrary to most people's expectations last week, the SEA market did not see a significant improvement this week, with the China direction notably weaker than the SEA direction. On Monday, it was heard that an SMX open in KSC fixed at 13K back to China, but it was said that the vessel required DD and had limited options. In the Aussie direction, some cargoes were still waiting to be covered, but offers were not aggressive, with a charterer calculating 20K for a Southeast Asia-based UMX. In the north, the general cargo segment was very active, especially for back haul cargoes to Africa or the Med. Vessels able to transit Goa could still get a decent premium. It was reported a charterer calculated 24k DOP for a UMX open in NChina. Early this week, it was also heard that a UMX fixed at 20K to WAfrica. Due to limited vessel supply, some charterers opted to take vessels on period basis. Several high period fixtures were seen this week, with levels reaching around 19kish for 1yr. The Nopac market was relatively less hot, but still felt to be rising, with many UMX vessels achieving around 18kish DOP for Nopac grain. In ECI, some vessels remains this week, with a UMX fetching around 16kish DOP for ECI cargo back to China. The WCI direction was generally flat. Some market cargoes emerged chasing vessels, but offers were limited, with a SMX for local WCI cargo back to China around 12K. The SAfrica market had considerable cargo volumes, with offers for a UMX for PACIFIC-bound cargo around 21K+210K. In summary, regional performance showed significant differences, with SEA flat but the north active. We look forward to seeing how the market performs going forward. As of May 11, the Richards Bay 6,000 kc NAR price was assessed at $118.04/t FOB, the highest since March. The weekly average reached $114.79/t FOB, marking the highest weekly average observed since November 2023. In the year to 6 May, South African coal exports rose 9.2% from the same period last year to 25.6 Mt, vessel tracking data show. ai_analysis.summary: 干散货市场延续升势，各船型指数全面上涨。Capesize大西洋航线表现强劲（C8+3,706美元），C3巴西-中国航线维持坚挺；Panamax 5TC突破21,000美元关口，太平洋市场信心改善；Supramax和Handysize稳中有升。FFA曲线前月合约大幅攀升，Cape May合约领涨市场，反应短期供需趋紧。

sections.title: Market Structure
sections.content: Capesize大西洋盆地上行信号明确，C8指数单日跳涨3,706美元至52,925美元，带动5TC综合突破46,000美元。太平洋C5航线相对平稳，但C3持续走强。Panamax大西洋fronthaul需求旺盛，太平洋即期运力趋紧，5TC录得693美元涨幅。Supramax和Handysize维持小幅上行态势。整体市场结构呈现大西洋领涨、太平洋跟进的格局。

sections.title: Dry Bulk Signals
sections.content: Cape C3合约出现$36.50实盘成交，印证$35-36价格区间支撑有效。Panamax澳洲航线固定价格达$24,000-29,000区间，为本周最高水平。FFA曲线前端涨幅领先，Cape May 26月合约跳涨3,275美元，Panamax Jun 26月涨2,700美元，远月Cal27同步跟涨。干散货市场短期基本面偏多，运价上涨趋势料延续。

sections.title: Trading Focus
sections.content: Cape C3和C8跨洋价差交易机会需关注，大西洋相对太平洋溢价扩大。Panamax太平洋5TC合约上方空间可期，建议关注P3A_82跨太平洋航线。Handysize亚区航线HS5、HS6维持升势，南美东海岸至北欧HS3航线单日涨205美元，反弹信号明确。FFA前端价差收敛提供套利窗口。

market_watch: Cape 5TC突破46,000美元阻力，短期目标48,000美元
Panamax 5TC站稳21,000美元，大西洋供需趋紧
C3巴西-中国航线$35.736，支撑$36.00整数关口
FFA前端涨幅领先现货，曲线backwardation收窄
Supramax太平洋S3西非航线单日跳涨350美元

route_focus.view: Tubarao至青島航线维持强势，$35.736报出，$36水平有实盘成交。大西洋至远东fronthaul需求强劲，短期支撑位$35.00，阻力$37.00。
跨大西洋航线从$14,573升至$18,118，fronthaul活动活跃。美国东海岸和南美东海岸需求突出，即期运力趋紧推动费率上扬。
Skaw-Passero至Rio航线报$7,132，跌54点。欧洲地中海区域运力充足，短期上行受限；建议关注南美东海岸反向航线HS3的反弹机会。
